route_dominance.statement: Let Q be the union of all valid reserves R(e) over active base pairs. Since Q is a subset of the M_B missing B-edges, |Q|>=D_B implies D_B<=M_B without a token matching, a root choice, or endpoint labels.
route_dominance.effect: Freezes fixed-endpoint LRH as the primary target. The complementary hard B branch is exactly |Q|<=D_B-1.

tight_deficiency_lemma.statement: In any finite colour-token incidence graph, if S is inclusion-minimal with |N(S)|<|S|, then |N(S)|=|S|-1 and N(S\{c})=N(S) for every c in S. Consequently every token of N(S) has at least two neighbours in S.
tight_deficiency_lemma.proof: For c in S, minimality gives |N(S\{c})|>=|S|-1. But N(S\{c}) is contained in N(S), while deficiency gives |N(S)|<=|S|-1. Equality holds throughout. The final assertion follows because deleting any one colour does not remove any token from the neighbourhood.
tight_deficiency_lemma.effect: Any Hall-style probe inside the root-free obstruction may restrict to a deficiency-one transversal circuit with no degree-one token.

actual_remaining_interface.branch_A: R_A=e(G[A_<q*])+I_mix(q*)-N_int(q*) must be absorbed by S_m or directly yield the colour target.
actual_remaining_interface.branch_B: Under |Q|<=D_B-1, the B-same and B-opposite normal-form regions remain live; Hall incidence is only auxiliary structure.
actual_remaining_interface.unified_target: Show that every typed cut with demand D_A-(M_B+S_m)>0 either violates a proved A/B budget or supplies Phi(n,e) pairwise-C7-compatible colours.
